identity.title: Submillimetre dust polarization and opacity in the HD163296 protoplanetary ring system
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper, we present ALMA observations of polarised dust emission of HD163296 at 870$\mu$m with a resolution of $\sim$0.2$\ensuremath{''}$ - sufficient to resolve the rings.

evidence.quote: Lying at a distance of 105pc[^2], it is classified as spectral type A2Ve, of age 5Myr (cite: Montesinos2009).
Sizes and luminosities in this paper have been revised based on the GAIA DR2 parallax

question.value: What are the polarisation fraction and angle structure and the 870/1300 um spectral index of the HD163296 ringed disk, and can self-scattering explain them?

evidence.quote: We present ALMA images of the sub-mm continuum polarisation and spectral index of the protoplanetary ringed disk HD163296.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.0.00616.S and #2013.0.00601.S.

evidence.quote: The calibrated data from the ALMA pipeline was examined, further flagging applied, and the individual executions were used to create self-calibrated solutions for the antenna phase and amplitude.
J1733-1304 was used as a flux calibrator with assumed fluxes of 1.52 and 1.67 Jy at 343.5 GHz on the two observing nights
A conservative calibration error is 7%, which would correspond to a spectral index offset of 0.3

imaged using CLEAN in CASA (cite: 2007ASPC..376..127M), producing separate images of Stokes I, Q, U and V

evidence.quote: Spherically symmetric dust grains are used, where the only source of polarisation is scattering (multiple scattering is included).

we use the radiative transfer code mcfost (cite: Pinte2006; Pinte2009)
The percentage polarisation (Fig.1b) ranges from 0.9% in the centre
with a median of 44.1$\pm1.5\ensuremath{^\circ}$ over the inner 30 au
giving $\alpha_{mm}$ of $2.1\pm0.3$

findings_qualitative.value: Polarisation fraction peaks (~4%) in gaps, anticorrelated with intensity; vectors become azimuthal in gaps

evidence.quote: It peaks in the gaps between the dust rings, and the largest value ($\sim\,$4$\%$) is found between rings 1 and 2.

claims.hypothesis: Self-scattering alone explains the polarisation pattern
claims.experiment: mcfost scattering model of ringed disk compared with ALMA 870 um polarisation
claims.result: Model reproduces major-axis enhancement, anticorrelation with intensity, minor-axis alignment and azimuthal twist in gaps
claims.finding: Consistent with self-scattering without additional alignment

evidence.quote: These general characteristics are consistent with a model of self-scattered radiation in the ringed structure, without requiring an additional dust alignment mechanism.

claims.hypothesis: Low alpha_mm in the inner disk is consistent with the polarisation-derived grain size
claims.finding: Dust/disk model needs refinement to match both

evidence.quote: further refinement of the dust or the disk model at higher resolution is needed to reproduce simultaneously the observed degree of polarisation and the low spectral index.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Magnetic or radiative-torque aligned grains do not predict minor-axis alignment in inclined disks

evidence.quote: for inclined disks like HD163296, they do not predict the same vector orientation along the minor axis in the centre

limitations_admitted.value: Ring widths unresolved so optical depth only a lower limit; absolute flux calibration may offset alpha by 0.3

evidence.quote: the ring brightness temperature only provides a lower limit to the optical depth, so we cannot discriminate between these possibilities

referee_caveats_inferred: Model comparison is qualitative, no fit or quantitative goodness
Band 6 and 7 epochs differ by a year, possible variability
